## User Feedback Analysis — 2026-08-16 (elizaOS)

### Data sources reviewed
- Discord summaries: 2026-08-13 to 2026-08-15 (very low technical volume on 08-15)
- GitHub issues/PR activity (month-to-date repo stats + top issues surfaced in aggregation)

---

## 1) Pain Point Categorization (Top recurring 5–7)

### 1) **Technical Functionality — Cloud agent provisioning reliability regressions (P0)**
**Frequency/Severity indicators**
- 1 of the top 5 surfaced GitHub issues is a quantified P0 provisioning regression: **16.1% hard failure** rate since 2026-08-06 (#18052), with a **~52 minute** failure feedback loop.
- Additional related thread: staging test coverage conflation with prod defaults (#18076).

**What users experience**
- Agent creation intermittently fails; failures can block future provisioning for the same org until fixed (#18052 references permanent lockout behavior pre-#17924).
- Users wait a long time before learning something failed (watchdog/retry loop → ~52 min).

**Concrete implementation opportunities (prioritized)**
1) **High impact / Medium difficulty:** Reduce time-to-failure-notification from ~52 min to <2–5 min  
   - Add early “capacity/placement preflight” + fast-fail on known 409/fence deadlock signatures (ties to #17924 + #18052).
2) **High impact / Medium difficulty:** Fix autoscaler ceiling/configurability + pre-warm behavior  
   - #18052 notes autoscaler gated by `maxNodes` hardcoded to 12 while 14 enabled; add env override + correct gating.
3) **High impact / Higher difficulty:** Add “provisioning invariants” monitoring + rollback automation  
   - Establish SLO alerts (failure rate, enqueue 409s, fence count growth, placement free slots) and automated rollback to last known-good daemon build.

**How similar projects address it**
- Kubernetes-based platforms often use admission controllers + preflight capacity checks to fail fast (clear, actionable errors) rather than letting async jobs time out.
- Managed CI platforms (e.g., Render/Fly-style deploys) surface “capacity unavailable” instantly and provide queue position/ETA.

---

### 2) **Performance — Auth/login first-interaction latency gated by provider list endpoint**
**Frequency/Severity indicators**
- 1 of top 5 surfaced issues: sign-in buttons gated by `/steward/auth/providers` taking **up to 4.7s in production** (#18049).

**What users experience**
- Login page paints quickly (FCP ~92ms) but cannot act until provider list returns; perceived as “site is slow/broken” at the first impression moment.

**Concrete implementation opportunities (prioritized)**
1) **High impact / Low–Medium difficulty:** Cache provider list with explicit TTL + safe invalidation  
   - If providers change only at deploy/config time, serve cached results (and document propagation).
2) **Medium impact / Medium difficulty:** Split “thin” auth bootstrap path from full app bootstrap  
   - Ensure the endpoint is served by a minimal code path with no upstream dependency chain (Worker-local response).
3) **Medium impact / Medium difficulty:** Add client-side optimistic rendering for common providers  
   - Render buttons for the default set immediately; reconcile with server response to avoid “dead” UI.

**How similar projects address it**
- NextAuth/Auth0-like flows commonly ship provider config as static JSON at build time or edge-cached with aggressive TTLs, so login stays interactive.

---

### 3) **Integration — Telegram onboarding/identity binding breaks end-to-end**
**Frequency/Severity indicators**
- 1 of top 5 surfaced issues: Telegram system bot onboarding is “dead” and does not bind Cloud identity (#17888).

**What users experience**
- Telegram DM returns onboarding URL, but:
  - URL points to a host that doesn’t reliably boot (`eliza.app/get-started` at the time of report).
  - Even when loaded via authenticated host as workaround, Telegram identity is not durably linked; user gets onboarding loop again on next DM.

**Concrete implementation opportunities (prioritized)**
1) **High impact / Medium difficulty:** Make Telegram linking cryptographically verifiable (server-validated Telegram proof)  
   - Do not treat browser auth as proof of Telegram sender; require signed Telegram payload/HMAC validation and persist canonical sender ID.
2) **High impact / Low difficulty:** Fix canonical onboarding URL configuration for Telegram bot  
   - Ensure `ELIZA_ONBOARDING_APP_URL` resolves to a working host that serves correct JS content types and caching behavior (#17888 notes MIME/caching inconsistencies).
3) **Medium impact / Medium difficulty:** Add E2E tests for “DM once → link → DM routes to agent”  
   - Include negative cases (expired token, replay, sender mismatch) as explicitly listed in #17888 acceptance criteria.

**How similar projects address it**
- Slack/Discord OAuth link flows typically complete linking in-chat with a signed “return to chat” token bound to the platform user ID (avoids “browser authenticated ≠ platform identity” confusion).

---

### 4) **Documentation / QA Process — Staging vs production coverage confusion**
**Frequency/Severity indicators**
- 1 of top 5 surfaced issues: a “green” live Cloud E2E job **silently targets production** by default and does not prove staging (#18076).

**What users experience**
- Maintainers/operators can believe staging is verified when only production is tested, leading to regressions reaching users or lingering staging breakages.

**Concrete implementation opportunities (prioritized)**
1) **High impact / Medium difficulty:** Separate staging/prod workflows with explicit base URLs + assertions  
   - Fail closed unless the resolved host matches `api-staging...` for staging lane.
2) **High impact / Low difficulty:** Add environment labeling to artifacts + job names  
   - Prevent “coverage inference” from a single lane.
3) **Medium impact / Medium difficulty:** Provision staging-scoped secrets + test credential route  
   - #18076 notes missing staging Environment secret inventory for required API keys.

**How similar projects address it**
- Many platforms enforce “environment-specific deploy + test contracts” (e.g., Vercel preview vs production) with hard-coded origin assertions and separate credentials.

---

### 5) **Community / Communication — Token migration window + governance/positioning uncertainty**
**Frequency/Severity indicators**
- Discord 2026-08-13: user missed token migration window and received no clear resolution path (omagles; AI16Z → ELIZAOS migration).
- Same day: multiple users expressed pessimism about token viability, governance confusion (Shaw detaching entity from token; foundation control), and asked for differentiation vs competitors (Hermes).

**What users experience**
- Unclear recourse for missed migration (support gap).
- Confusion about who controls what (brand vs foundation vs server).
- Lack of crisp value proposition narrative in 2026 competitive landscape.

**Concrete implementation opportunities (prioritized)**
1) **High impact / Medium difficulty:** Publish a “Token migration & support policy” page (FAQ + escalation path)  
   - Include: eligibility, deadlines, whether any remediation exists, and where to open a ticket.
2) **High impact / Medium difficulty:** Publish governance/ownership clarification (roles, permissions, who operates infra)  
   - A single canonical statement reduces rumor-driven churn.
3) **Medium impact / Medium difficulty:** Publish “elizaOS vs alternatives” positioning doc focused on framework capabilities  
   - Tie differentiation to shipped features (voice barge-in, visual workflow studio, connector ecosystem, cloud runtime model).

**How similar projects address it**
- Web3-adjacent OSS projects that survive turbulence often separate “product roadmap & governance” comms from day-to-day chat, with pinned canonical docs and periodic summaries.

---

### 6) **Community / Onboarding — Channel fragmentation & unanswered newcomer questions**
**Signals from Discord**
- Question: “Is there a Telegram chat channel?” (kenxybruck, 2026-08-14) went unanswered in the provided segment.
- New members joining are welcomed (lychee, 2026-08-15), but technical routing (“where do I ask X?”) is not evidenced.

**Concrete implementation opportunities**
1) **Low difficulty / Medium impact:** Add a pinned “Where to ask what” message + support pathways (Discord + GitHub)  
2) **Medium difficulty / Medium impact:** Decide on Telegram presence (official vs none) and document it  
3) **Low difficulty / Medium impact:** Add “newcomer triage” rotation to ensure basic questions get responses

---

## 2) Usage Pattern Analysis (Actual vs intended)

### Observed “actual usage”
- **Cloud-hosted onboarding and agent provisioning** is a dominant operational focus (issues #18052, #18076, #18049).
- **Messaging-first entry** (Telegram/iMessage/Discord DM → connect → agent replies) is a primary real-world flow (#17888 and related onboarding continuity work referenced across the repo activity).
- **Voice as a production feature** is positioned as important (weekly summary notes real-time voice in production; community member satya.manhas expects multi-platform apps).
- **Community discussions drift into tokenomics/governance** when product comms are quiet (Discord 08-13).

### Gaps vs intended usage
- Intended: smooth onboarding across surfaces; actual: identity binding and environment routing issues cause loops (Telegram onboarding repeats).
- Intended: staging validates changes; actual: staging lane can be “green” while hitting prod defaults (#18076).

### Emerging/unexpected use cases
- **DAO/crypto/payments collaboration** interest (Zeroclaw community call; paralens.ai shared) suggests users want deeper integration with on-chain analytics and payments tooling.
- **Brand/naming experimentation** (rename suggestion “XOS”) is likely lighthearted, but signals attention to identity/positioning.

### Feature requests aligned to usage patterns (from signals)
- Cross-platform chat + voice parity (Discord expectations of Android/iOS/Mac/PC apps).
- Multi-channel community comms (Telegram chat request), though needs clear stance to avoid support fragmentation.

---

## 3) Implementation Opportunities (Solutions per major pain point)

### A) Provisioning reliability (16.1% failure) — #18052
- **Ship first:** preflight capacity + fail-fast + actionable UI/console error copy (Impact: very high, Difficulty: medium)
- **Next:** autoscaler ceiling/env overrides + prewarm nodes (Impact: high, Difficulty: medium)
- **Then:** fleet fencing cleanup and deadlock prevention (Impact: high, Difficulty: higher)

### B) Login interactivity (4.7s gate) — #18049
- **Ship first:** edge caching/provider-list TTL + explicit invalidation (Impact: high, Difficulty: low–medium)
- **Next:** “thin endpoint” serving path (Impact: medium–high, Difficulty: medium)

### C) Telegram onboarding/identity binding — #17888
- **Ship first:** signed Telegram proof + durable external identity link (Impact: high, Difficulty: medium)
- **Next:** correct canonical host and asset MIME/cache behavior (Impact: high, Difficulty: low–medium)
- **Then:** E2E coverage for positive + negative cases (Impact: medium–high, Difficulty: medium)

### D) Staging coverage honesty — #18076
- **Ship first:** explicit environment base URL + assert host + separate jobs (Impact: high, Difficulty: medium)
- **Next:** staging secrets/credential route + fail closed without them (Impact: high, Difficulty: medium)

### E) Token/governance support gap — Discord 08-13
- **Ship first:** publish canonical policy docs + link from Discord pins (Impact: medium–high, Difficulty: low–medium)
- **Next:** provide a single intake form for migration/support requests (Impact: medium, Difficulty: low)

---

## 4) Communication Gaps

### Expectation mismatches observed
- **“Staging is tested” vs reality:** current workflows can pass while exercising production defaults (#18076).
- **“Linking my Telegram means my agent will reply in Telegram” vs reality:** onboarding loop repeats and identity binding doesn’t persist (#17888).
- **“Holding token means I’m safe” vs reality:** missed migration window has unclear remediation; governance/ownership uncertainty amplifies frustration (Discord 08-13).

### Recurring questions implying onboarding/docs gaps
- “Is there a Telegram chat channel?” (Discord 08-14)
- “What can I do if I missed token migration?” (Discord 08-13)
- “What makes elizaOS unique vs competitors like Hermes?” (Discord 08-13)

### Specific documentation/onboarding improvements
- Add a **single “Onboarding flows” doc** mapping: DM platform → web auth → identity link → agent assignment → first reply (with diagrams).
- Add a **“Staging vs Production” operator doc** describing environment URLs, secrets, what each lane actually proves, and how to validate manually.
- Add a **“Project positioning in 2026”** page focused on framework capability differentiation (not token).

---

## 5) Community Engagement Insights

### Power users & their needs (from GitHub + surfaced issues)
- **standujar**: high-signal operational QA; provides quantified regressions and acceptance criteria (#18052, #18049, #18076). Needs: faster operator feedback loops, unambiguous environment separation, reliable provisioning.
- **lalalune / NubsCarson / wtfsayo**: heavy contributors on reliability, CI hardening, onboarding and connector UX. Needs: clearer product priorities, structured issue intake, and reduced churn from environment/flow ambiguity.

### Newcomer friction signals
- New users are welcomed (lychee), but the dataset shows **minimal technical guidance** or routing to “first steps,” and basic questions can go unanswered (Telegram channel question).

### Converting passive users into contributors
- Create a **“good first issue” track** tied to onboarding/docs diagrams and small connector UX fixes.
- Introduce a **weekly community triage hour**: pick 3 issues (one cloud, one connector, one docs) and pair newcomers with maintainers.
- Encourage “repro-first” contributions by templating HAR capture + minimal repro scripts for onboarding/login issues.

---

## 6) Feedback Collection Improvements

### Current channel effectiveness
- **GitHub issues are highly actionable** (quantified metrics, repro steps, acceptance criteria).
- **Discord is currently low-signal for product feedback** on some days (08-15 had no technical content), and important questions may not be answered (08-14 Telegram channel query).

### Improvements to gather more structured feedback
1) Add a **single pinned Discord intake link**: “Report a bug / onboarding loop / provisioning failure” → GitHub issue form with required fields (environment, platform, host, timestamps).
2) Add **in-product “Report onboarding problem”** button on `/login` and `/get-started` that exports redacted diagnostics (host, request IDs, timing).
3) Run a **monthly structured survey** for:
   - onboarding success rate (by connector),
   - login perceived latency,
   - provisioning success rate and time-to-agent.

### Underrepresented segments whose feedback is missing
- **Non-Discord users** (Telegram/iMessage-first users) who may churn without filing GitHub issues.
- **Mobile-only users** (Android/iOS) given expectations of app support but limited direct feedback in this dataset.
- **Framework builders (non-crypto)**: Discord discourse skewed toward token/governance; need clearer channel for OSS/framework adoption feedback.

---

## Prioritized High-Impact Actions (Next 2–4 weeks)

1) **Provisioning reliability hotfix plan**: reduce agent provisioning failures toward <1% rolling 7-day and cut failure notification from ~52 minutes to <5 minutes (targets #18052 acceptance direction).  
2) **Make staging coverage honest**: split staging/prod E2E lanes, assert target host, and add staging-scoped credentials so “green” means “staging proven” (#18076).  
3) **Fix Telegram onboarding end-to-end**: canonical working onboarding URL + server-validated Telegram identity binding + E2E tests for “DM → link → DM routes to agent” (#17888).  
4) **Login time-to-first-action improvement**: cache or thin-path `/steward/auth/providers` to eliminate multi-second sign-in gating in production (#18049).  
5) **Publish two canonical comms docs**: (a) token migration/support policy and (b) “what is elizaOS in 2026 / differentiation” to reduce recurring Discord uncertainty (Discord 08-13 threads).

# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Aug 9 - 15, 2026)

## Executive Summary
This week, the ElizaOS project focused on hardening our infrastructure and unifying our cloud presence to ensure a more stable, production-ready experience. By consolidating our platform and integrating new visual tools, we have significantly improved both the reliability of our agents and the ease with which users can build and manage them.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Unifying the Cloud Experience**
_Goal: We aimed to simplify how users access and manage their agents by consolidating our cloud services into a single, cohesive platform._
- We successfully migrated Eliza Cloud to `eliza.app` ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18996)), creating a streamlined hub for account management and login.

**Enhancing Agent Performance and Reliability**
_Goal: We wanted to ensure that agents start faster and operate more consistently, especially when handling media or voice interactions._
- We reduced agent "cold-start" wait times by optimizing how our systems handle shared data ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18762)).
- Real-time voice features, such as dynamic greetings and interruption support, were moved into production to provide a more natural interaction experience ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/19655)).
- We improved system stability by ensuring hardware resources are managed more intelligently ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18639)).

**Empowering Creators with Visual Tools**
_Goal: We are making it easier for users to design complex agent behaviors without needing to write extensive code._
- We integrated the `smthrs` visual workflow studio ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/19000)), allowing users to build and edit agent workflows through a visual interface.

**Strengthening Security and Safety**
_Goal: Protecting our users and their data is a top priority as we scale our infrastructure._
- We implemented new security guards to prevent unauthorized data access when agents process images or audio ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18716)).
- We addressed a critical security vulnerability in a document-processing dependency to keep the framework secure ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/18873)).

## Repository Spotlights

### elizaos/eliza

# Overall Project Monthly Summary (August 2026)

## Executive Summary
In August 2026, ElizaOS focused on strengthening the foundation of our AI agent framework by improving system reliability and formalizing community contributions. By hardening our infrastructure and initiating a shift toward a more modular architecture, we have set the stage for more scalable and stable agent development.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Strengthening System Reliability and Safety**
_Goal: We aimed to make our AI agents more predictable and robust, ensuring they handle errors gracefully and maintain data integrity._
- Improved agent safety by ensuring that when tools fail, the system avoids providing generic, unhelpful responses ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17490), [elizaos/eliza#17501](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17501)).
- Enhanced the stability of agent startup and shutdown processes to prevent data loss or database corruption ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17531), [elizaos/eliza#17180](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17180)).

**Modernizing Infrastructure and Development Workflows**
_Goal: We focused on streamlining our internal tools to help developers build and test the framework more efficiently._
- Hardened our automated testing pipelines to prevent regressions and ensure consistent performance across different operating systems ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17526), [elizaos/eliza#17552](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17535)).
- Improved the reliability of our testing environment by isolating memory and voice latency checks ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17513)).

**Empowering Community Collaboration**
_Goal: We wanted to create a transparent and rewarding environment for the contributors who drive our project forward._
- Launched the `eliza.army` leaderboard and tracking system, providing a clear way to recognize and incentivize community development efforts ([elizaos/eliza](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17326)).

## Repository Spotlights

### elizaos/eliza
- Launched the `eliza.army` contribution tracking system ([elizaos/eliza#17326](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17326)) to formalize and reward community engagement.
- Initiated a strategic move toward modularity by planning the extraction of core components into standalone repositories ([elizaos/eliza#17568](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17568), [elizaos/eliza#17569](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17569)).
- Optimized CI/CD pipelines by removing outdated workflows ([elizaos/eliza#17528](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17528)) and improving Windows compatibility ([elizaos/eliza#17526](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17526)).
- Refined the mobile UI experience by fixing notification animation issues ([elizaos/eliza#17518](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17518)) and mandating semantic OCR coverage for better visual testing ([elizaos/eliza#17581](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/pull/17581)).
- Addressed ongoing maintenance tasks, including work on Bun runtime unification ([elizaos/eliza#17044](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17044)) and troubleshooting UEFI boot failures ([elizaos/eliza#17222](https://github.com/elizaos/eliza/issues/17222)).

The fix (#17745, republish the org-balance gate hint after a debit) has been on `develop` since before this cycle; production is the only place it has not landed.\n\nAlso shipping, user-facing:\n- **App-mode onboarding** (#17752): logging in on `app.elizacloud.ai` lands in *your* dedicated agent — automatic entry, chooser, resume, error fallback. Evidence: live before/after captures, walkthrough video, OCR review on the PR.\n- **Cross-origin SSO** (#17788): one login across the dashboard and app origins — atomic single-use codes on Postgres, fail-closed logout, PKCE binding; hardened after security review.\n- **Fired reminders deliver their content** (#17776), never a bare acknowledgement.\n- **Node embedding sidecar** (#17787): provisioning installs it, health-checks probe it, self-heal converges the fleet — closing the \"sidecars wiped again\" regression loop.\n- Latency hot-path work (#17743 lineage) and the rest of 448 commits of fixes.\n\nAlso shipping, operational: the certification pipeline itself was restored and made runnable (#17790, #17792, #17794, #17796–#17799, #17802 — the workflows had been deleted by an accidental sweep, and the chain had never run end to end; it now produces the signed certification this PR carries, and caught a real unlisted-public-route gap in review).\n\n## Migrations (5 new, all additive + idempotent — audited)\n\n| Migration | Shape |\n|---|---|\n| `0164_pooled_credentials` | 2 new tables + indexes, all `IF NOT EXISTS` |\n| `0185_job_execution_interruptions` | `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (integer, default 0) |\n| `0186_agent_sandbox_physical_name_indexes` | 2 partial indexes, `IF NOT EXISTS` |\n| `0187_agent_sandbox_lifecycle_revision` | guarded column + `CREATE OR REPLACE` function + trigger replace (`DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` → recreate — idempotent pattern) |\n| `0188_sso_bridge_store` | 2 new tables + index, all `IF NOT EXISTS` |\n\nNo destructive ops, no data rewrites, no `DELETE`/`TRUNCATE`/table drops anywhere in the set.\n\n## Certification\n\n`certification.json` at the repo root + signed evidence bundle at `evidence/bundle/`, produced by the `certification-hosted` workflow on the promoted commit: deterministic scenario lane (226 artifacts) + the develop-pr test recipe (`run-all-tests.mjs --only=test --no-cloud --concurrency=3`) recorded as the matrix lane, analyzed, rolled up, Ed25519-signed against the repo trust anchor, self-verified green before upload.\n\n## Post-deploy verification (will be run and posted here)\n\n1. Billing probe: 8 consecutive inference calls — expect 8/8 ok (was 4/8)\n2. Latency: raw inference timing before/after\n3. `/api/v1/admin/agent-image-canary` — expect present (was 404)\n4. Control-plane deploy → sidecar self-heal converges all 8 nodes\n5. Onboarding walk on app.elizacloud.ai + SSO bridge across origins\n\n\n## Test proof at promotion (GitHub Actions major outage at promotion time)\n\nThe certified recipe (`build:core` + `build:views` + `run-all-tests.mjs --only=test --no-cloud --concurrency=4`) executed locally at `acf5fe75b4e` on the operator VPS: **123 package suites passed, 6 failed — every failure individually adjudicated, zero unexplained:**\n\n| Local failure | Adjudication |\n|---|---|\n| app-core (guard) | REAL #17859 fallout: browser view missing from both desktop catalogs — **fixed in #17864** (8/8 green) |\n| scenario-runner (guard) | REAL #17859 fallout: two new history-recall scenarios unclassified in the coverage map — **fixed in #17864** (17/17 green) |\n| app-core (supervisor ×2) | environment-here: real-process spawn timeouts on this host; the robot certification run 31073689058 executed this exact suite green |\n| vault | environment: headless host, no session bus (\"keychain bypassed: host unsafe\") — same class documented in #17818 |\n| agent (early-logs) | environment: TTY color leak into captured stderr — documented in #17818 |\n| plugin-calendar | environment: PGlite WASM init hook timeout under load — documented in #17818 |\n| ui (flick + render bench) | environment: timing/benchmark under load; suites green across the PR gates that merged this code |\n\nEvery failing suite above is additionally green in GitHub's clean CI on the PRs that introduced this code. #17864 (two guard-map fixes, no runtime code) merges post-outage and rides the next promotion.\n\nThe signed certification re-dispatches the moment GitHub Actions recovers and lands as the allowed post-signing artifact. Deploy is dispatched on recovery (workflow_dispatch, environment=production).\n",
